meanings.note: Expressive conversational Russian interjection or greeting ('hi') used directly in spoken exchanges.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'пойти'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'from here'.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Everyday conversational Russian name meaning 'Vika', frequent in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вика, Паша! Как я рад. Проходите, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Vika, Pasha! I'm so glad. Come in, please.

examples.text: Вика, ты на какой машине сегодня приехала?
examples.trans: Vika, which car did you come in today?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ходу').

сработать.gloss: to work, succeed; to go off

meanings.en: to work, be effective, succeed (of a plan)
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'работать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to work, succeed; to go off', paired with 'срабатывать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to go off (of an alarm)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Не сработает, но мужику жизнь испортим!
examples.trans: It won't work, and we'll ruin the man's life!

examples.text: Надеюсь, эта безумная авантюра сработает сегодня.
examples.trans: I hope this crazy gamble will work today.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'plan' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The mayor came up with a new plan.

examples.text: Но мэр придумал новый план. Сосед мэра теперь пойдёт в мэры.
examples.trans: But the mayor came up with a new plan. The mayor's neighbour will now run for mayor.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'молчать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fall silent, shut up', paired with 'молчать'.

examples.trans: Shut up and stop frightening us.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('please') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('you're welcome') (answer to thanks) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('here you are') (handing something over) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'портить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to spoil', forming an aspectual pair with 'портить'.

examples.text: А я испорчу отношения с будущим мэром.
examples.trans: And I'll ruin my relationship with the future mayor.
